newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon to accelerate T$400 bln project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon to accelerate T$400 bln project.

text.p: Taiwan's microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co said on Wednesday it plans to accelerate its planned 10-year T$400 billion expansion project due to rising demand.
"Due to rising demand, we plan to accelerate our T$400 billion project originally scheduled to be completed within 10 years," a company spokesman told Reuters.
"But this is based on the premise that if our profit return is good, we will complete the project within six to seven years," he said by telephone.
The firm's board also decided to invest an additional T$3.32 billion to expand capacity of its existing plants, he said.
In April, Taiwan Semicon said it would build six advanced wafer-fabrication plants as part of a T$400 billion investment at southern Taiwan's Tainan Science-based industrial park over a 10-year span.

Rival United Microelectronics in June announced plans to invest T$500 billion in a 10-year wafer project -- making it Taiwan's largest single industrial project -- raising the stakes in the island's integrated circuit war.
Several other chipmakers followed suit to announce similar projects with investment ranging between T$100-200 billion.
Taiwan Semicon's foundry business does not design and sell its own IC products, but custom-makes them according to customers' specifications.

The IC foundry business has found a niche as more and more IC design companies worldwide -- which do not have microchip production capability because of the high cost of investing in the business -- are emerging with new designs to catch up on developments in the computer world.
